before: Promise.all(iterable) returns a promise for an array of fulfilled values in input order. If an input rejects, the result rejects with a rejection reason; this does not cancel the other operations. It is useful when every result is needed.

Promise.allSettled(iterable) waits until every input settles and fulfills with records in input order. A fulfilled record has status and value; a rejected record has status and reason. It does not turn a failed operation into a successful one: it preserves the failure as data.

The result arrays follow input order, not whichever operation happens to finish first. Empty input produces an empty array. Optional practice: reverse the two supplied promises and predict the returned record order before running.
after:
`Promise.all` waits for every input to succeed. It returns their values in input order.

If one input fails, the combined Promise fails too. This does not cancel the other work. Use it when you need every result to succeed.

`Promise.allSettled` waits for every input to finish, whether it succeeds or fails.

It returns a record for each input. A successful record has `status: "fulfilled"` and a `value`. A failed record has `status: "rejected"` and a `reason`.

Complete `settledLabels(promises)`. Await `Promise.allSettled(promises)` and use the supplied mapping to make the labels.

Keep input order, even if operations finish in a different order. Empty input returns an empty array. This exercise uses text values and text failure reasons.

before.question: If the rejecting input is replaced by Promise.resolve("B"), what does Promise.all produce?
choices: A rejection because the array once contained a rejected promise.
A fulfilled promise containing ["A", "B"] in input order.
Only "B", because all keeps the final completion.
before.explanation: Both supplied inputs now fulfill, so all can fulfill with their ordered values; it does not remember a prior array from another run.
